A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Q2D2 research work. Their complete main texts, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original Q2D2 reconstruction, semantic classification, listening-study, ablation, mutual-information, and reconstruction-speed results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds downstream text-to-speech evaluation, broader semantic classification results, and a sampling-rate/token-rate study.

M1.justification: Section 3, Equations 1–5, and Algorithms 1–3 retain the projections, tanh bounding, feature pairing, grid construction, nearest-point quantization, and straight-through gradients. The new TTS experiment uses the existing codec representations without establishing a change to Q2D2 itself.

E1.justification: Table 7 expands ARCH evaluation from four speech datasets to ten datasets, adding MTT, MS-DB, ESC50, US8K, FSD50K, and VIVAE. v2 also evaluates downstream TTS on LibriTTS, which v1 identified as future work. The listed codec-training corpora remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The revised CMOS comparison in Table 6 includes DAC alongside WavTokenizer and Q2D2, whereas v1's reconstruction CMOS table included only WavTokenizer and Q2D2 plus ground truth. This is a limited comparator addition within the replacement TTS experiment; the objective reconstruction and ARCH comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The reconstruction CMOS evaluation on LibriSpeech/LJSpeech is replaced by LibriTTS TTS evaluation using a 600M ParlerTTS setup, with ground truth now reported at zero. Appendix D also introduces a sampling-rate/token-rate sweep with other hyperparameters reportedly fixed. Its highest-rate condition is unclear: the prose specifies 16/24/48 kHz, while Table 13 lists 16/24/24 kHz. Existing reconstruction protocols otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds sensitivity analysis of reconstruction quality across sampling/token rates, and Section 4.1 adds brief memory and latency profiling across quantization settings. The previous grid, dimension, level, projection, offset, gradient, and mutual-information analyses are retained. The original reconstruction-speed comparison is relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains identical MUSHRA scores and ± values, while both versions' CMOS tables report point estimates. No new seed counts, repeated training-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear. The newly specified listener counts are protocol documentation rather than a changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds six ARCH result columns, including Q2D2 accuracies of 0.2847 on MTT and 0.4241 on US8K, plus sampling-rate results and memory/latency ranges. Its new TTS CMOS-Q/CMOS-P scores are -0.11/-0.22 for Q2D2, -0.22/-0.36 for WavTokenizer, and -0.05/-0.10 for DAC. These replace reconstruction CMOS results under different conditions, not same-setting performance changes. Retained objective reconstruction, MUSHRA, original ablation, and RTF values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds an explicit lattice-distance comparison in Equations 6–8, including rectangular and rhombic spacing expressions, and argues that midpoint connections reduce maximum quantization error at fixed grid-point count. v1 contained qualitative packing discussion but not this calculation. The original quantizer equations and hexagonal-offset derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract broadens its competitive-to-superior reconstruction-performance claim from speech to speech, audio, and music. This substantially expands the stated domain of the main empirical claim, although the added non-speech results concern semantic classification. The central quantization contribution and numbered contributions remain largely unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning suitability for autoregressive TTS, semantic generalization beyond speech, and scaling to higher token rates, while elaborating the rhombic-grid mechanism. Appendix E removes v1's qualifications about unevaluated TTS and limited music/general-audio evaluation, although the conclusion still calls audio/music future work. Existing reconstruction and utilization interpretations are largely retained.

D1.justification: The front-page audio-samples link is replaced by a code-repository link. v2 specifies the 600M ParlerTTS implementation and documents at least ten listeners per sample, low-pass anchor construction, headphones, a quiet environment, and listener training. These disclosures do not establish that the unchanged MUSHRA results were rerun. Conversely, the explicit LibriTTS-only training statement for the semantic experiment is removed.

R1.justification: Selected sources change substantively: the Chen/El-Nouby product-quantization citations are replaced by Jégou et al. (2011), and codebook discussion introduces Zheng and Vedaldi (2023) and Zhu et al. (2025). The F-measure citation also changes to Sasaki (2007). Overall positioning relative to FSQ, VQ, RVQ, and neural codecs remains stable; many other reference edits are bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, author order, and front matter, adds acknowledgements and an impact statement, and makes localized prose revisions. Reconstruction speed moves into Appendix D, with subsequent appendix renumbering. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a single-column to a two-column layout, substantially resizing and relocating tables, figures, and algorithms. The reconstruction bubble plot is removed while its underlying table results remain; the mutual-information figure is retained and renumbered. Table 7 gains six columns, Table 6 is restructured for TTS, Table 13 is added, and several ablation tables drop their redundant Model column.

improvement.justification: The TTS and non-speech semantic experiments address part of v1's explicitly deferred validation, while fuller listening-study documentation and a code link improve reproducibility information. These benefits are limited by the sampling-rate inconsistency and the abstract's broader audio/music reconstruction claim, which the added classification results do not directly establish. With the codec and original numerical results unchanged, the evidence supports a useful but limited net improvement.
